previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for acute worsening of chronic diastolic heart failure, presenting with dyspnea, chest pain, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema. Initial concern for ACS was ruled out with normal cardiac biomarkers and EKG showing no acute ischemia. A chest X-ray showed stable cardiomegaly without acute findings. He was treated with IV furosemide, leading to symptom improvement and weight reduction. His warfarin was held due to a supratherapeutic INR of 3.7 and later restarted at a reduced dose. Glyburide was held in favor of insulin during admission, with plans to resume at home. Eosinophilia was noted but found to be a chronic finding on review of records. He was discharged home in stable condition with increased diuretic therapy, medication adjustments, and follow-up plans including a cardiac stress test.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with weakness and nausea.  Study to evaluate for
acute process.

COMPARISON:  ___.

SINGLE PORTABLE RADIOGRAPH:  A left chest wall cardiac pacemaker/AICD is in
place with leads terminating in the right atrium and right ventricle.  Median
sternotomy wires are intact.  

There is mild bibasilar dependent atelectasis.  Within limitation of low lung
volumes, there is no focal consolidation.  There is no pleural effusion,
pulmonary edema, or pneumothorax.  Mild cardiomegaly is stable.  Mediastinal
and hilar contours are within normal limits.  There are no acute osseous
abnormalities.


IMPRESSION:  No evidence of acute cardiopulmonary process.  Stable mild
cardiomegaly.

INDICATION:  ___ man with weakness, nausea, and elevated liver
function test.  Study to evaluate for cholecystitis or obstruction.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen from ___.

FINDINGS:  The liver is diffusely echogenic, consistent with hepatosteatosis. 
There is no focal liver lesion.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary
dilatation.  The gallbladder is nondistended and does not contain stones. 
There is no pericholecystic fluid or gallbladder wall thickening.  The common
duct measures 2 mm.  There is hepatopetal flow within the portal vein.  There
is no evidence of ascites.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of cholelithiasis or cholecystitis.
2.  Diffuse echogenic liver most likely represents hepatosteatosis.  However
other forms of advanced liver disease such as fibrosis or cirrhosis cannot be
excluded.

INDICATION:  ___ male with mechanical aortic valve replacement, low
INR, altered mental status, slurred speech.  Question of stroke.

COMPARISON:  Head CT of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axially acquired images were obtained through the head without
contrast.

FINDINGS:  There is no acute hemorrhage, large areas of edema, large masses or
mass effect.  Prominence of the ventricles and sulci is likely due to age-
related parenchymal atrophy.  Gray-white matter differentiation is preserved.
Periventricular white matter hypodensities are consistent with chronic small
vessel ischemic changes.  There is no evidence of a vascular territory
infarct. There is stable dolico ectasia of the right intracranial vertebral
artery.

Visualized paranasal sinuses are clear.  There is partial opacification of the
inferior right mastoid air cells.  Remainder of the mastoid air cells are
clear.  Soft tissues of the nasopharynx and visualized orbits are within
normal limits.  

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial process.  Findings consistent with chronic
small vessel ischemic changes.  No evidence of acute vascular territory
infarct.
